writtenTo: The people of Israel and Judah
importantNotes: Micah 5:2 prophesied the Messiah's birth in Bethlehem — fulfilled 700 years later.
Micah 6:8 is considered one of the greatest ethical summaries in all of Scripture.
'Who is a God like you, who pardons sin?' (7:18) — a play on Micah's own name.
Micah was a contemporary of Isaiah, Hosea, and Amos.
The book alternates between judgment oracles and promises of salvation.

chapters.1: Judgment announced against Samaria and Jerusalem for their sins.
chapters.2: Woe to those who exploit the poor and steal land; a remnant will be gathered.
chapters.3: Corrupt leaders, false prophets, and unjust judges condemned; Zion will be plowed like a field.
chapters.4: The mountain of the LORD will be exalted; swords into plowshares; God will reign.
chapters.5: The ruler from Bethlehem — the Messiah; He will be great to the ends of the earth.
chapters.6: God's lawsuit against Israel — 'what does the LORD require? Act justly, love mercy, walk humbly.'
chapters.7: Micah laments the corruption but trusts in God — 'Who is a God like you, who pardons sin?'
